property_summary: After calling Put(_unlockTime) by any account sending any value, the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime in the correct contract is >= block.timestamp (it never becomes earlier than the current block time); the mutant that uses _unlockTime < block.timestamp ? _unlockTime : block.timestamp can set unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs and thus violate this invariant.

For any call to Put by any address with any payable amount, the reference contract always stores Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it never sets unlockTime earlier than now); the mutant that uses the reversed ?: can store a past unlockTime (unlockTime < block.timestamp) for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, after calling Put(...) the reference contract always stores Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp (it never sets unlockTime earlier than now); the mutant that flips the ?: can set a past unlockTime (< block.timestamp) for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this invariant.

After calling Put(_unlockTime) with any sender and any nonzero msg.value, the reference C always sets Acc[sender].unlockTime to either _unlockTime if it's in the future, or to the current block.timestamp; the mutant that reverses the ?: can set Acc[sender].unlockTime to a value strictly less than block.timestamp when the attacker supplies a past _unlockTime, violating the invariant that unlockTime is never less than block.timestamp for accounts that deposited funds.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and any deposit value, if Put is called then the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime is either equal to block.timestamp or equal to the provided _unlockTime when that _unlockTime is in the future; the mutant that flips the ?: can set unlockTime strictly less than block.timestamp for some inputs, violating that the recorded unlockTime is never strictly in the past when a deposit occurs.

Invariant: calling Put with any msg.value never reverts due to addition overflow in the reference (because it checked for overflow via require) — the mutant (which removed the require) can revert on inputs where acc.balance + msg.value overflows under Solidity 0.8 semantics (causing an automatic revert) and thus breaks the invariant for some fuzzed balances/values.

For any caller and any payable amount, calling Put never reverts (reference enforces safe addition so Put always succeeds for admissible inputs); the mutant removing the explicit overflow check can cause an overflow-revert for some combination of prior stored balance and msg.value, causing Put to revert.

For any caller and any payable amount (within uint256), calling Put does not revert in the reference because it checks for overflow before adding msg.value to balance; the mutant removes that check and can cause an overflow revert for some prior stored balance and msg.value, so Put may revert there.

For any caller and any payable amount msgValue where the caller's prior stored balance plus msgValue does not overflow uint256, calling Put(...) always succeeds (does not revert) on the reference; removing the explicit require can make Put revert for some prior balances and msgValue that cause addition overflow, so the mutant can fail while the reference never does for inputs constrained to avoid trivial under/overflows — we ensure admissible inputs by bounding msgValue to avoid trivial overflow in the reference but allow the mutant to still revert when prior stored balance is large.

For any caller and any msg.value (0..type(uint).max) when calling Put on the reference, the call never reverts (the reference always accepts deposits); the mutant that removed the pre-check can revert for some combinations of prior stored balance and msg.value that overflow uint256, so the mutant may cause Put to revert while the reference never does.

For any caller and any deposit value, after calling Put(...) the contract's recorded acc.balance for that caller increases exactly by the deposited msg.value (so address(c).balance == sum of deposits and Acc[caller].balance reflects deposited sums); the mutant incorrectly adds an extra +1 wei to the stored balance causing Acc[caller].balance to be greater than the actual funds deposited for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit amount >= MinSum, after calling Put the stored Acc[caller].balance equals the total wei actually sent to the contract (no extra phantom +1 wei); the mutant that adds +1 breaks this because stored balance will exceed actual deposited sum for some fuzzed inputs.

For any depositor and any deposit amount, the contract's stored per-address balance (Acc[depositor].balance) is always less than or equal to the contract's actual on-chain balance (address(c).balance); the mutant that adds +1 wei to the stored per-address balance can make the stored balance exceed the contract's actual balance for some inputs.

For any depositor and any msg.value, after a single Put call by that depositor the recorded Acc[depositor].balance equals the previous stored balance plus msg.value (i.e., Put increments stored balance by exactly msg.value); the mutant that adds +1 breaks this because it increments stored balance by msg.value+1 for some fuzzed inputs.

For any depositor and any deposit amount, after calling Put(...) the stored Acc[depositor].balance equals the cumulative sum of msg.value values actually recorded by the contract for that depositor (i.e., when depositing X in a single Put call starting from zero balance, Acc[depositor].balance == X); the mutant that adds +1 wei to the stored balance breaks this by making Acc[depositor].balance == X+1 for some fuzzed X.

For any caller and any supplied _unlockTime, after Put(...) completes the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime in the reference equals max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) (i.e. it never decreases below current block.timestamp or the provided later time); the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp violates this when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any caller and any provided _unlockTime and deposit, after Put finishes the contract stores Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp and equals _unlockTime when _unlockTime > block.timestamp; the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp violates this for inputs where _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any caller and any provided _unlockTime and deposit, after Put completes the reference contract stores Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp and if _unlockTime > block.timestamp then Acc[caller].unlockTime == _unlockTime; the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp violates this for inputs with _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any caller depositing via Put with a chosen _unlockTime, the reference contract ensures Acc[caller].unlockTime is at least block.timestamp and if _unlockTime is strictly in the future then Acc[caller].unlockTime equals that _unlockTime; the mutant that overwrites unlockTime to block.timestamp violates this whenever _unlockTime > block.timestamp (so there exists inputs with future _unlockTime that make stored unlockTime different).

For any caller and any provided _unlockTime and deposit value, after Put completes the reference stores Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp and if the provided _unlockTime is strictly in the future then Acc[caller].unlockTime equals that provided _unlockTime; the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp violates this for inputs where _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any caller and any msg.value, after Put returns the most recent Log.LastMsg recorded by the reference contains the same msg.value just deposited (log observes the new deposit amount), whereas the mutant that logs before updating balance can cause LastMsg.Val to reflect a state inconsistent ordering (i.e., the log is emitted before the balance update) and thus differ for some inputs (re-entrant or observing order); we detect this by asserting that after Put the LogFile.History's last entry Val equals the sent amount.

After any successful Put by any caller with any msg.value>0, the Log contract's last recorded message Val equals the amount sent (the reference logs after updating state so the external log observes the deposited amount), whereas the mutant that calls LogFile.AddMessage before updating acc.balance can cause the recorded Val to not reflect the final deposited effect for some inputs (exposed by a reentrant attacker that triggers Put via fallback).
Collect cannot transfer out funds exactly at the recorded unlockTime (i.e., a Collect that succeeds must happen only when block.timestamp > the stored unlockTime).

Collect should not revert when called at or after an account's unlockTime if the account has enough balance and meets MinSum; specifically, if Collect reverts at block.timestamp >= unlockTime then the preconditions must not have held.

property_summary: Collect only reverts at the unlock boundary when the caller's recorded unlockTime is strictly less than the current block timestamp (i.e., if Collect reverts when called at time T then the caller's unlockTime is strictly greater than or equal to T).

Collect should succeed (not revert) exactly when the caller's stored unlockTime is strictly less than the current block timestamp, given sufficient balance and MinSum — i.e., at the instant equal to unlockTime behavior differs and must be disallowed.

If Collect is invoked and the call reverts, then either the amount is below MinSum or the contract's recorded unlockTime for the caller is greater than or equal to the current block timestamp (i.e., Collect only reverts when caller is not strictly past unlockTime or balance constraints fail).

For any caller, when block.timestamp == acc.unlockTime the reference C disallows collection (Collect reverts/does not send) but the mutant allows collection at the inclusive boundary; hence the invariant is that at exact unlockTime a Collect attempt that would succeed only at that boundary must fail on the reference but can succeed on the mutant.

For any actor and amounts, if a holder's balance >= MinSum and >= requested amount, then at the exact block timestamp equal to their unlockTime a Collect call must NOT succeed on the reference (requires strictly greater), but the mutant (using >=) can allow success — so the invariant is: a Collect initiated when block.timestamp == acc.unlockTime always fails on the reference; the mutant can make it succeed for some inputs.

For any caller, amount and unlock time, if Collect is invoked exactly at block.timestamp == acc.unlockTime and the holder has sufficient balance >= MinSum and >= requested amount, then the reference contract refuses to transfer funds (Collect does not succeed), while the mutant may allow the transfer because it uses >= for the time check.

For any caller with a funded account (balance >= MinSum) and a requested amount <= their balance, if Collect is invoked at a timestamp equal to their unlockTime the correct contract C must refuse to send funds (Collect does not succeed) while the mutant that uses >= may succeed; thus the rule: a Collect call at block.timestamp == acc.unlockTime always does NOT transfer funds (returns/behaves as failure) on the reference but the mutant can succeed for some inputs.

For any caller, amount and unlockTime where the holder has balance >= MinSum and >= amount, invoking Collect exactly when block.timestamp == unlockTime must NOT succeed (the reference requires strict >), whereas the mutant using >= can allow the Collect to succeed for some inputs.
If an account's balance is below MinSum then Collect cannot withdraw any funds (no change in contract balance) — i.e., Collect only sends value when pre-call balance >= MinSum.

property_summary: If Collect reverts when called with amount _am, then the caller's stored balance must have been less than the requested amount or the unlock time has not passed (i.e., Collect only succeeds when account balance >= _am and unlock time < block.timestamp).
Collect only succeeds (does not revert) when the caller's recorded balance is at least the requested amount and the caller's unlockTime has passed.
If calling Collect does not revert, then the caller's stored balance must be at least the requested amount and their unlockTime must be strictly less than the current block timestamp.
If the call to Collect does not revert, then the caller's stored balance must be at least the requested amount and their unlockTime must be strictly less than the current block timestamp.
